step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identify raw data landing in the S3 Input bucket, triggering events into High and Low priority SQS queues depending on application type and required latency.
2. EC2 Worker Nodes retrieve task messages from SQS queues and query the Resource Manager (running on EC2) to obtain available EMR cluster endpoints.
3. The Resource Manager queries and stores mapping data in RDS, while using CloudWatch to monitor state and handle recovery of spot instance EMR clusters.
4. EC2 Worker Nodes submit processing jobs directly to the dynamically assigned spot EMR clusters.
5. EMR clusters execute the big data processing tasks and persist output results back to the S3 (EMRFS) destination bucket.

nodes.notes: Holds lower-priority batch processing task messages.
